<!-- pr-reviewer: 34eb46055bf3c3d3c3c119b0edc19571b8b67eda -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge**

**What looks good**
- The fix is one guard in `stock_grid` (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs:99-100`): `tool_r` is replaced by 0 only when it is not finite. Every program with a real cutting tool passes a finite radius, so `auto_cell` gets exactly the value it got before. The lattice cannot coarsen or shift for those programs.
- The plan is empty only when every op is a probe (`plan_program`, `stock_sim.rs:~290`, the `ToolKind::Probe` `continue`). Any cutting op pushes a `Planned` or returns an `Err` by name (lost toolpath, no sane cone/corner, rotary/lathe refusals). An empty plan therefore cannot hide a program that cuts, and the sim keeps judging every real cut.
- A degenerate stock still refuses by its own name. A missing stock gives "no stock ..." and a rotated stock gives its rotation message, both before the new line. A bad box still hits `Dexel::from_shape` ("finite positive dx, dy, dz"). `auto_cell` in the sim crate is untouched.
- Provenance and the test header are present, the decision record sits in `docs/decisions/`, and the body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #592`. `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main; the merge was clean)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| probe_only_sim | 2 passed |
| post_not_judged | 4 passed |
| stock_sim_document | 9 passed |
| setup_carry | 9 passed |
| carried_verify | 8 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| probe_op | 11 passed |
| sim | 4 passed |
| stock_play | 7 passed |
| stock_stamp | 4 passed |
| stock_engine_agreement | 3 ignored (heavy lane) |
| `--lib stock_sim` | 7 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

No golden or snapshot changed. `stock_grid` is also called from `rest.rs` and `rest/across.rs` with `fold(tool_r, f64::min)`; those start from the consumer's own finite radius, so they are unaffected.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The guard tests `is_finite()`, not "plan is empty". A tool whose radius is NaN or infinite would previously have been refused as an invalid setup. It is now judged on a span-sized lattice. That is arguably better, and the per-op sanity checks refuse nonsense tools earlier. If you want it strict, make the guard depend on the empty plan, for example in `walk` at `stock_sim_carry.rs:205`.
2. `a_probe_only_program_without_a_stock_still_says_why` passes when `not_judged` is empty (`probe_only_sim.rs:~75`), because of the `if !line.is_empty()` branch. It pins "never the wrong cause" but not the by-name refusal. Asserting `line.contains("no stock")` unconditionally would pin it. Not a blocker.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 534f628fa811f1efb0e33070ff86e0fdd68b9a39 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge**

Re-review of the delta since 34eb4605 (2 files: `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`, `crates/app/tests/probe_only_sim.rs`), trial-merged with fresh upstream/main (clean, no conflicts).

**What looks good**
- `stock_sim.rs:101`: the lattice falls back to the span only when `tool_r == f64::INFINITY` (the empty fold). Any finite radius reaches `auto_cell` unchanged, so non-probe programs size exactly as before.
- `probe_only_sim.rs`: the no-stock test now uses `.expect(...)` on `not_judged` and asserts `contains("no stock")`, so it can no longer pass vacuously.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| probe_only_sim | 2 passed |
| post_not_judged | 4 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| stock_sim_document | 9 passed |
| setup_carry | 9 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The comment at `stock_sim.rs:98-100` says a NaN or negative radius "reaches `auto_cell` and is refused by name". `auto_cell` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cut.rs:35`) does not refuse: `f64::max` ignores NaN and a negative value is clamped up to 1e-4/span. Behaviour for those inputs is the same as before this PR, so nothing regresses, but the comment overstates it. Consider rewording to "behaves as before".

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
